note: The public, versioned capability-tag registry for the operator-blind background-task mechanism (ADR 0021). A capability tag is the OPAQUE token that rides the job envelope and the worker's claim on the wire and in the DB, so a bare database dump sees `02f271ff`, not `grant-delivery`. Each tag value is the first 4 bytes (8 lowercase hex chars) of SHA-256 over `veyq/v1/task-capability/<name>` — deterministic, no central assignment authority, extensible. This keeps gratuitous plaintext semantic labels out of the store (defence vs. a bare dump); it does NOT hide the kind of work from a correlating operator (that residual leak is correlation-bounded, documented in ADR 0021 and docs/crosscutting/background-tasks.md). Both surfaces (backend Kotlin, web TS) pin these exact values; a conformance test asserts the shipped constant equals the registry, the same drift-proofing the crypto vectors get.

grant-delivery.description: Deliver a scope grant to a pending (grant-less) member: any online key-holder wraps K_SC to the target member's identity public key (asymWrap to a foreign identity, context `scope-grant`) and posts the ciphertext as that member's wrappedGrant. Universal tag; like every job it is completed only by the worker holding its lease (ADR 0021 §6), and a repeated completion is a no-op (idempotent, first-online-wins). The first, trivially-blind consumer of the mechanism (ADR 0020).

scope-rotation.description: Complete a queued scope-key rotation that the event causing it could not perform (en.spaces.scope-key-rotation §E1, uc.spaces.complete-queued-rotation). One server-side originator: a tenant-member removal that cut a co-shared GROUP membership (the removing owner is not necessarily a key-holder there, ADR 0025 — groups rotate). An account rotation after a compromise queues none: the rotator mints its scopes' next epochs itself (ADR 0060 Decision 4). Unlike grant-delivery this is NOT reconcilable from DB state, so the pending-rotation state is recorded explicitly as this job (resourceRef == scopeId). Offered only to an OWNER of the scope (the only member who may commit a rotation, ADR 0021 §4); the owner reads the directory after its claim, mints E_{n+1} + wraps E_n + re-grants the surviving member set on-device (POST /api/scopes/{scopeId}/epochs), then completes. An event joins a job only while it is pending, so removals before anyone is online coalesce into one rotation, and an event after a claim gets a job of its own. Like every job it is completed only by the worker holding its lease (ADR 0021 §6), and only once that holder committed an epoch during the lease; first-online-wins. Operator-blind: opaque tag + scopeId + the resulting ciphertext epoch-link/re-grants — the server never mints, wraps, or holds a key.
